main_text.l: ergo secuti partes ad superiores literas

l.i: I. Perquàm gratæ mihi tuæ acceptæq; extiterunt
literæ.
II. Nam & animum in me benevolum prom-
ptumq; declararunt: & verò adhortationem conti-
nuerunt longè saluberrimam.
III. Respondissem ad eas citius, nisi te nescio quo
profectum esse audivissem.
IIII. Neque enim officium in te ullum sine ma-
gna ἀχαριστίας[?] reprehensione intermittere me posse
intelligo.
V. Et quidem rei huius causas habeo plurimas &
maximas: vel paternæ amicitiæ: vel meæ in te obser-
vantiæ: vel deniq; beneficiorum, quæ in me hactenus
contulisti, & adhuc confers quotidie.
VI. Itaq; etiam atq; etiam rogo, hoc tibi persua-
deas, unum te esse, quem parentis ego loco colam:
& in quo spem meam omnem fixam locatamq; ha-
beam.
VII. Operam me quoq; daturum: ut tua apud
me monita, & prudentiæ, & fidelitatis plena, eum
quem debent locum inveniant: nec in capessenda
Rep. officio defuisse meo cuiq; videar.

page.notes: The text is cut off at the right edge of the scan, so the line ends of the last paragraph are not visible beyond "Per-". The Greek word in IIII. is hard to read: the printed form looks like ἀχαεισίας or ἀχαρισίας; I have transcribed it as ἀχαριστίας with a doubt mark. The ff in "Refpondiffem", "nifi" and "audiuiffem" is a double long s, rendered as ss. The line "Conclusio" is printed as "Con" at the line end and "clusio" on the next line, with no hyphen, so it is written whole. The space after "Ciceronis." is missing in the print, and I have kept it that way.
